title: yadgar/iam-db
$comment: CLOSED PER CHART (ADR-0847, ADR-0850, ledger 990): this schema closes every key iam-db's own values.yaml declares and refuses an unknown one at render. It closes only what this chart owns -- a parent or platform that embeds iam-db leaves this whole section open instead of re-declaring it. OPEN MAPS, left as `{}` on purpose: `global` (injected by a parent/platform at render time; this chart reads none of it itself, but a closed root would refuse the key the moment it is embedded); `resources` and `database.instance.resources` (plain Kubernetes ResourceRequirements, handed straight to `toYaml`, whose own shape is not this chart's to validate); `rollingUpdate` (same, handed to `toYaml` under `strategy.rollingUpdate`). EXTRAS, declared as leaves though `values.yaml` never states them: `image.digest` (absent from `values.yaml` by design -- `ci-release` rewrites it at package time, D65); `networkPolicy.scrapeFrom.namespace` (`values.yaml` ships `scrapeFrom: {}`; `templates/networkpolicy.yaml` reads the key under it). TYPES, TOGGLES AND `required` ON A NEW KEY ARE NOT THIS FILE'S JOB (ADR-0847): `chart/templates/render-checks.yaml` validates `database.create` and `autoscaling.enabled` with `kindIs "bool"` and raises its own named refusal; nothing here duplicates that. `database` carries `type: object` and `required: [migrationLockTimeoutSeconds, engineOperatorReserve, acquireTimeoutSeconds, idleTimeoutSeconds, maxLifetimeSeconds]` (ledger 814, ADR-0837, ADR-0849, card C-DB2): each of these five knobs is a leaf this file bounds as a typed `integer` with a `minimum` (and, for `migrationLockTimeoutSeconds`/`acquireTimeoutSeconds`, a `maximum`), because the binary reads every one of them with no fallback. There is no root `required`: `database` deleted outright is still refused by the chart's own render check (`database` is absent from the values), with a more specific sentence than a schema line would give. `tls.enabled` IS a typed, required exception to the 'types/toggles are not this file's job' rule (C-DB1, ADR-0845, K-8, K-3): it is a LEAF, so ADR-0847's carve-out for a value `render-checks.yaml` guards (a block the schema deliberately leaves untyped) does not apply to it the way it does to `database.create` or `autoscaling.enabled` -- `templates/render-checks.yaml` still carries the named sentence a bare schema refusal would not give, but the schema's own `required`/`type: boolean` is what reddens `helm lint --strict`, which a template-only `fail` cannot (K-3). `tls.clientAuth` is `required` with no default since B-U5 (X-ADR-1), because the binary refuses to boot without the variable it renders, but it stays UNTYPED: its type and value are `templates/render-checks.yaml`'s job (ADR-0847), so a bare `off` meets the named sentence rather than a generic schema line. `tls.clientCaSecret` and `tls.clientCaSecretKey` stay EXTRAS (B-U5E; `values.yaml` states neither).

enabled.description: No default (H1 of the ADR-0705 census, ADR-0845): absent used to mean cleartext, which is the silent downgrade this `required` and `type` refuse together. `templates/render-checks.yaml` carries the named sentence; this is what reddens `helm lint --strict`, which a template-only `fail` does not.

clientAuth.description: No default (X-ADR-1, extending ADR-0845; card B-U5): it renders LISTEN_TLS_CLIENT_AUTH, which iam-db refuses to boot without whether or not TLS is on. `required` here and deliberately UNTYPED (ADR-0847): `templates/render-checks.yaml` refuses a non-string (a bare YAML off is the boolean false), a value outside `off | optional | required`, and a verifying mode beside `tls.enabled: false` or with no `tls.clientCaSecret`, each with a sentence naming the key. A schema `type` or `enum` would pre-empt those sentences with a generic line.

engineOperatorReserve.description: Headroom inside engineMaxConnections reserved for an operator, a backup job or a monitoring agent (ADR-0849). Rendered as DB_ENGINE_OPERATOR_RESERVE and read with no fallback: `yadgar-store` v0.4.0 deleted the `5` it used to compile in. Minimum 1: zero leaves a non-admin operator no way into a full engine (`store` refuses it too).

acquireTimeoutSeconds.description: Seconds `acquire` waits for a free connection before failing. Rendered as DB_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS and read with no fallback (ADR-0837); replaces sqlx's own 30s default. Maximum 29: below the CALLER's own dial REQUEST_TIMEOUT (30s) -- this process never dials out, so the budget it has to stay under is the caller's (iam's), not its own -- so a stalled acquire can never be the deadline a caller's whole request runs against (card C-DB2; see tests/chart_request_deadline.rs). Minimum 1: zero fails every acquire that has to wait.

idleTimeoutSeconds.description: Seconds an idle connection is kept before the pool closes it. Rendered as DB_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS and read with no fallback (ADR-0837); replaces sqlx's own 600s default. Minimum 1: zero closes connections as fast as the pool opens them.

maxLifetimeSeconds.description: Seconds at which a connection is retired however busy it is. Rendered as DB_MAX_LIFETIME_SECONDS and read with no fallback (ADR-0837); replaces sqlx's own 1800s default. Minimum 1: zero retires every connection the instant it opens.

migrationLockTimeoutSeconds.description: Seconds a replica waits for another one's migration before failing its boot. Rendered as DB_MIGRATION_LOCK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS and read with no fallback. Minimum 1: GET_LOCK with 0 never waits and with a negative wait never takes the lock. Maximum 590: see chart/values.yaml.
